---
title: "3. Meet the inputs: Your own study"
---

## Locate the three files

| File in `data/my-study/` | What to inspect |
|---|---|
| `feature-counts.tsv` | Feature IDs in rows; sample IDs in columns; integer read counts |
| `sample-metadata.tsv` | One row per sample, with sample ID, group and available covariates |
| `taxonomy.tsv` | Each feature ID and its supplied lineage or display label |

Pick one sample and find it in counts and metadata. Pick one feature and find
it in counts and taxonomy. Row order is not evidence of a match; IDs are.

Create the folder and files if absent. Start with actual read counts; do not
round proportions, microarray intensities or normalized abundance into counts.
If biological taxonomy is unavailable, repeat unique feature IDs as labels
and record that limitation.

Preserve participant, visit, site, batch, medication and other design fields
where available. Document source, assay, preprocessing and exclusions. Use
nonidentifying IDs. A valid file format cannot establish independent samples.

**Your task:** record assay, sample unit, group definition and one missing piece of information that matters for interpretation.
